title: GPX Viewer: See Tracks, Routes and Waypoints
description: Open a GPX file and see its tracks, routes and waypoints drawn in the browser with the GPX Viewer — parsed locally, never uploaded. Free.
summary_sentence: The viewer draws supported GPX tracks, routes and waypoints with default styles and shows approximate statistics.
quick_answer: The GPX Viewer draws a GPX file's tracks, routes and waypoints on a map, entirely in your browser. Drop the file and see what it actually contains — geometry, waypoint names and all — before trusting it in a device, a report or your boots.
steps_intro: Files lie by filename. The map shows the truth:

An export that looks wrong in a platform looks wrong here first — swapped coordinates and truncated tracks confess visually in seconds.

use_cases.title: Sharing a route with a group

body.t: Open the file, screenshot the map, send. Recipients see the plan without installing anything; waypoints ride along with their names.

use_cases.title: Auditing a client's or club's archive

body.t: A folder of legacy GPX becomes a browsable collection — files that draw nothing announce their emptiness before any deeper tool wastes time.

examples.label: Example · The route that was a track

body.t: A file named 'route.gpx' draws as a dense, wiggly line with thousands of points — a recording, not a plan. The viewer makes the family obvious; the counters (
) then put numbers on what your eyes already know.
A trail drawn in the sea off the coast means longitude and latitude were swapped somewhere upstream. The viewer cannot fix it, but it turns a silent data bug into a visible one in two seconds.

popular_table.note: The viewer also displays timestamp span and raw elevation statistics when available. GPX exports can omit timestamps and extensions.

faq: Yes, when enough plotted line points have elevation. The profile is a simplified display and raw elevation can be noisy.
The map is empty but the file has size.
Size can be metadata, extensions or a waypoints-only file with points off-screen — zoom to the points using the GPX Bounding Box Tool's extent, or check for zero tracks with the counters.
Names are shown in the feature list and properties popup, not as permanent labels on the map.
Why does my track look angular?
Sparse recording: points every 10–30 seconds draw as chords. The shape is the file's sampling, faithfully shown — not a viewer simplification.
No. The viewer uses the same default line style for tracks and routes.
A file from a very old GPS?
GPX 1.0 files draw the same way — the geometry elements predate the 1.1 revision.
The drawn map is yours to capture — a viewed, verified route picture beats a filename in any report.
